# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Knee Arthroscopy / Meniscus Surgery (CPT 29881)

**Governing Policy:** Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet (Evolent_CG-316) — https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2024-02/2023%20Knee%20Arthroscopy%20Clin%20Tip%20Sheet%20Evolent%2002282024.pdf

**Member:** Emerson Hayes
**Member ID:** W807153430
**Plan:** Harvard Pilgrim Health Care (Commercial/ACA), Massachusetts
**Denial date:** 2026-08-04
**Reference number:** POC-9668BA39E4-60948

---

Dear Harvard Pilgrim Health Care Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881), which was denied on 2026-08-04 (reference number POC-9668BA39E4-60948). The denial states that my records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I do not believe that conclusion is supported by my own records or by the plan's own tip sheet, and I am asking that this decision be reconsidered. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary.

**Duration and nature of my symptoms.** I have had progressive knee pain for 12 months that has not improved with rest. Imaging on 2026-05-24 showed a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking. I experience locking and giving way, cannot squat or kneel, and am limited to level walking. On examination, I had positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion. The plan's tip sheet states that "[t]he guidelines should be reviewed for additional requirements including duration of symptoms, physical examination, and radiographic criteria and for the complete listing of other procedures not included below." My records document all three of these elements: 12 months of symptom duration, a positive physical exam, and MRI findings of a displaced, mechanically significant tear.

**Conservative treatment already completed.** The tip sheet lists non-operative measures for related procedures, including "quadriceps strengthening and appropriate hamstring/IT band stretching and patellar mobilization techniques," along with "oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics, tramadol," "Physical therapy modalities," "Supervised home exercise," and "Corticosteroid injection." My records show that I completed 24 visits of supervised physical therapy over 14 weeks (2026-03-30 to 2026-07-06) focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, took NSAIDs for 6 months without adequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-23 that gave only two weeks of partial relief. This is not an absence of conservative care — it is a documented course of the same categories of treatment the plan's own tip sheet describes, without lasting improvement.

I also note that the specific non-operative duration thresholds quoted in the tip sheet (6 months for lateral release, 12 weeks for patellofemoral chondroplasty) apply to different procedures than the one requested. The tip sheet itself states that it does not provide "the complete listing of other procedures not included below," which suggests that a displaced bucket-handle meniscal tear with mechanical locking may not be governed by those two listed thresholds at all. I ask that the plan clarify which specific criterion within Evolent_CG-316 applies to CPT 29881 for a locked meniscal tear, and confirm that it has been applied to my complete record.

**Imaging and arthritic changes.** My MRI showed articular cartilage that is preserved, with a Kellgren-Lawrence grade of 1. The tip sheet states that "MRI should not be the primary tool used to determine the presence or severity of arthritic changes in the joint," and its own grading table describes grade 1 as only "[p]ossible joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation" — the mildest category, well short of moderate or severe arthritic change. My surgery is being requested because of a mechanical tear causing locking and instability, not because of arthritic joint changes, so any concern about arthritis severity does not apply to my situation.

**Request.** I am asking that Harvard Pilgrim reconsider this denial in light of the conservative treatment I have already completed and the mechanical findings documented on MRI, and that it identify the specific criteria within Evolent_CG-316 that apply to my requested procedure so that my records can be evaluated against the correct standard. I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-01-31, and I am submitting it by phone at 1-888-333-4742 (Member Services) and to the appeal address printed on my denial letter.

Please let me know if any additional records from Dr. Marchetti's office or my physical therapy provider would help complete this review.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

Emerson Hayes
Member ID: W807153430
[Mailing address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
